surname_desc: Jin (陳) is around Korea's 48th most common surname at about 0.3%. The Yeoyang Jin clan traces to a Song Chinese official who settled in Goryeo; the sound is crisp and memorable.

short: Someone graceful as silk, standing tall like a mountain
meaning: 라준 (羅峻, Rajun) joins 라 (羅, ra), "silk, to spread out," with 준 (峻, jun), "lofty and towering." It's a boy's name meaning someone graceful as silk, standing tall like a mountain. The 준 syllable is among the most beloved, as in 민준 (Minjun); the 라 opening adds exotic polish — a distinctive yet upstanding impression.
surname_desc: Kang (姜) is Korea's 8th most common surname at about 1.3%. The Jinju Kang clan traces back to Kang I-sik, a legendary founder of the ancient Goguryeo era, and produced the celebrated general Kang Gam-chan.

short: Someone wise who stands tall like a mountain
meaning: 예준 (叡峻, Yejun) joins 예 (叡, ye), "bright and wise," with 준 (峻, jun), "lofty and towering." It pictures someone wise who stands tall like a mountain. In recent years 예준 has topped Korea's boys'-name charts — 예 signals wisdom, 준 is the most loved ending (민준, Minjun; 서준, Seojun). Wisdom and height meet in a polished, quintessentially modern name.
surname_desc: Kim (金) is Korea's most common surname, held by about 21.5% of the population — roughly one in five Koreans. The major lineages, the Gimhae and Gyeongju Kim clans, trace back to Silla royalty.

short: Someone graceful as kindness
meaning: 나은 (娜恩, Naeun) joins 娜 (beautiful) and 恩 (grace), a pairing that carries the quiet hope that a person will move through the world with beauty while treating others with a generous, gentle heart. It wishes for beauty that is never cold, only kind. Spoken aloud, it flows softly — open vowels, a light bounce between syllables — na-eun easing off the tongue with familiar simplicity for new ears to hold.
surname_desc: Kang (姜) is Korea's 8th most common surname at about 1.3%. The Jinju Kang clan traces back to Kang I-sik, a legendary founder of the ancient Goguryeo era, and produced the celebrated general Kang Gam-chan.

short: Someone clever who unfolds soft as silk
meaning: 리라 (悧羅, Rira) joins 리 (悧, ri), "clever and bright," with 라 (羅, ra), "silk, to spread out." It's a girl's name meaning someone clever who unfolds soft as silk. It evokes the lyre and lira, an exotic ring. Flowing with no final consonants, it gives an elegant, musical, international impression.
surname_desc: Ko (高) is Korea's 22nd most common surname at about 0.9%. The Jeju Ko clan is legendary — one of the three founding families said to have emerged from the earth on Jeju Island.

short: Wisdom given lasting, steady foundation
meaning: 지건 (智建, Jigeon) joins 지 (智, ji), meaning wisdom, with 건 (建, geon), meaning to establish, painting the hope that one builds a life on deep, thoughtful understanding rather than fleeting cleverness—wisdom made sturdy, given form and foundation. Spoken aloud, the name feels soft yet crisp, opening on that clear "ji" sound before settling into the grounded, open vowel of "geon," like a gentle step followed by a firm plant of the foot. Abroad, it echoes easily into the familiar English name Deacon, giving it a comfortable, natural landing in new company.
surname_desc: Lee (李) is Korea's second most common surname at about 14.7% of the population. Its most famous lineage, the Jeonju Lee clan, founded the Joseon Dynasty and ruled Korea for over 500 years.

short: Someone precious as a pearl and graceful
meaning: 주아 (珠雅, Jua) pairs 주 (珠, ju), "pearl, jewel," with 아 (雅, a), "elegant and refined." It pictures someone precious as a pearl and graceful. Soft and stylish, 주 carries jewel-value while 아 (as in 수아, Sua) is a top-loved ending. Preciousness and grace meet in a lovely, trendy name.
surname_desc: Heo (許) is Korea's 29th most common surname at about 0.6%. Legend holds the Gimhae Heo clan descends from Queen Heo Hwang-ok, an ancient princess said to have sailed from India to marry King Suro.

short: Someone bright and of high character
meaning: 대성 (旲聖, Daeseong) joins 대 (旲, dae), "great light," with 성 (聖, seong), "virtuous and saintly." It pictures someone bright and of high character, and sounds like 대성하다, "to achieve greatly," for a note of success. K-pop fans may think of BIGBANG's Daesung — a bright, dependable, warmly familiar name.
surname_desc: Ahn (安) is Korea's 17th most common surname at about 1.3%. Meaning 'peace,' it's borne by national heroes like independence activist Ahn Jung-geun — the Sunheung Ahn clan is its main lineage.

short: Mountaintop, the highest point in native Korean
meaning: 마루 (Maru) — above all, this is the native Korean word for "mountaintop, the highest point (sky)." The characters 마 (瑪, "agate") and 루 (婁, "star") echo beneath, but the native meaning leads: someone who shines like a star from the highest place. Round and spirited with no final consonants, it's a bright, beloved boy's name with a fresh native ring.
surname_desc: Song (宋) is Korea's 18th most common surname at about 1.3%. The Eunjin Song clan was a pillar of Joseon Confucian scholarship, producing the eminent scholar Song Si-yeol.

short: A name of silk and kindness
meaning: 라은 (羅恩, Raeun) joins the silk-soft unfurling of 라 with the warm kindness carried in 은, and together they paint a hope: that goodness will spread outward gently, the way silk ripples open with a single motion, never forced. It is a name wishing for a heart that gives freely and gracefully. Spoken aloud, it feels light and clear, its open vowels unfolding easily on the tongue — soft, crisp, unhurried. Abroad, it settles comfortably beside Lark, sharing a bright, airy lift in sound.
surname_desc: Jeong (鄭) is Korea's fifth most common surname at about 4.3%. Its major clans (Dongnae, Yeonil) produced renowned scholars and statesmen throughout the Goryeo and Joseon dynasties.

short: Someone warm who excels
meaning: 온유 (溫愈, Onyu) pairs 온 (溫, on), "warm," with 유 (愈, yu), "kind and gentle." It's literally the word 온유하다, "gentle and tender." Soft from the very sound, it suits boys and girls alike, and K-pop fans will think of SHINee's Onew. Familiar too from the Beatitudes' "blessed are the meek," it's a warm, beloved name whose kindness comes through directly.

short: A helper who leads with steady care
meaning: 우솔 (佑帥, Usol) joins 우 (佑, u), meaning to help, with 솔 (帥, sol), meaning leader, painting the hope that someone would grow into a person who guides and shelters others, a helper who leads by steady care rather than force. Spoken aloud, the name flows smoothly, its open vowels giving it a soft, crisp brightness, gentle yet clear, not unlike names such as 시우 or 한솔. Abroad, it settles easily beside the name Orson, familiar on the tongue while carrying its own distinct identity.
surname_desc: Bae (裵) is Korea's 26th most common surname at about 0.7%. The Seongju Bae clan descends from one of the six village chiefs who legendarily founded Silla.
